jen: Heads-up PR #3605 (API guide: max_tokens & truncation examples) is blocked. Reviewer wants exact wording on how the runtime handles responses that exceed `max_tokens` and whether the SDK appends ellipses or returns a partial chunk. Also docs-preview failed fetching runtime metadata (403). Tagging @omar and @li for runtime/SDK confirmation.

omar: Link to PR?

jen: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/3605. The example shows `max_tokens: 256` and a streaming snippet that cancels via AbortController; reviewer asked: if a request hits the server-side max, do we close the stream with a final chunk, or do clients see an abrupt termination? Also they want to know if SDKs will append any indicator (like "...") to show truncation.

ci-bot: docs-preview job #672 failed: error fetching runtime metadata (403). Logs: /builds/3605/logs/672.

li: Runtime note: when a model-generation reaches the server-side `max_tokens` limit the runtime closes the stream cleanly and returns `status: "truncated"` in the final delivery envelope (not an HTTP error). There is no automatic textual ellipsis added by the runtime. Clients may see the last token boundary as-is.

omar: SDK note: JS and Python SDKs surface the final envelope as `response.truncated === true` (or similar) on completed responses, and they do NOT mutate the text by adding ellipses. For streaming, the stream closes normally; if a client aborts mid-stream, the SDK will surface an `aborted` error state and will not mark the result as truncated. Docs should be explicit: server truncation = clean close + metadata flag; client abort = abort error, no truncation flag.

jen: Great. For the preview 403, can we avoid calling the live metadata endpoint in the snippet? I'll replace the live fetch with `const runtimeInfo = { env: 'PREVIEW_STUB' } // preview-only` and add the explicit sentence about truncation vs abort.

li: Confirmed runtime behavior, approve wording. Also recommend a short migration note: "If you relied on an ellipsis previously, update parsers to check `response.truncated` or stream end status."

ci-bot: retriggered docs-preview #672 (attempt 2).

ci-bot: docs-preview #672 succeeded.

jen: Requested reviewer re-approval and scheduled merge for today's window.

omar: Approved.

jen: Merged in window. Leaving a follow-up to add a tiny FAQ entry about `response.truncated` handling in SDKs. :white_check_mark:
